title: Impact of China's WTO Accession on Manufacturing Employment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
**Difference-in-Differences (DID)** is the appropriate method. We compare manufacturing employment changes in high-trade-exposure regions (treated) versus low-trade-exposure regions (control) before and after China's 2001 WTO accession. The key assumption is **parallel trends**: absent WTO accession, treated and control regions would have experienced similar employment trends.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s34_data.csv")

# Basic summary statistics
print("=== SUMMARY STATISTICS ===")
print(summary(data))

# Check balance of treatment groups
print("\n=== TREATMENT GROUP BALANCE ===")
print(table(data$treated, data$post))

# Main DID regression with unit and time fixed effects
print("\n=== MAIN DID RESULTS ===")
did_model <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = data)
print(did_model)

# Extract and print the key coefficient
did_coef <- coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"]
did_se <- se(did_model)["treat_x_post"]
print(sprintf("\nMain DID Coefficient: %.4f (SE: %.4f)", did_coef, did_se))

# Alternative specification without fixed effects for comparison
print("\n=== SIMPLE DID (NO FIXED EFFECTS) ===")
simple_did <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = data)
print(summary(simple_did)$coefficients)

# Robustness check: Pre-treatment means comparison
print("\n=== PRE-TREATMENT BALANCE CHECK ===")
pre_treatment <- data[data$post == 0, ]
pre_means <- aggregate(y ~ treated, data = pre_treatment, FUN = mean)
print(pre_means)
diff_pre <- pre_means$y[2] - pre_means$y[1]
print(sprintf("Pre-treatment difference: %.4f", diff_pre))

# Parallel trends check (visual and statistical)
print("\n=== PARALLEL TRENDS CHECK ===")
trends_data <- data %>%
  group_by(treated, period) %>%
  summarise(mean_y = mean(y), .groups = 'drop')

print(trends_data)

# Create time trends plot
p <- ggplot(trends_data, aes(x = period, y = mean_y, color = factor(treated))) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Period", y = "Mean Log Manufacturing Employment", 
       color = "Treatment Group",
       title = "Parallel Trends Check") +
  scale_color_discrete(labels = c("Control", "Treated")) +
  theme_minimal()
print(p)

# Statistical test for pre-treatment trends
if(length(unique(data$period)) > 2) {
  print("Multiple periods detected - running trend test")
} else {
  print("Only 2 periods - basic difference test")
  pre_diff_test <- t.test(y ~ treated, data = pre_treatment)
  print(sprintf("Pre-treatment t-test p-value: %.4f", pre_diff_test$p.value))
}

# Robustness: Clustering standard errors by unit
print("\n=== ROBUST STANDARD ERRORS (CLUSTERED BY UNIT) ===")
did_robust <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
                   data = data, cluster = "unit_id")
print(did_robust)

# Final summary
print("\n=== FINAL RESULTS SUMMARY ===")
print(sprintf("DID Estimate: %.4f", did_coef))
print(sprintf("Standard Error: %.4f", did_se))
print(sprintf("95%% Confidence Interval: [%.4f, %.4f]", 
              did_coef - 1.96*did_se, did_coef + 1.96*did_se))

# Economic interpretation
percent_change <- (exp(did_coef) - 1) * 100
print(sprintf("Percentage change in manufacturing employment: %.2f%%", percent_change))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a **negative coefficient** of approximately **-0.15 to -0.30** for the DID estimator. China's WTO accession likely increased import competition in manufacturing sectors, particularly affecting regions with high trade exposure. The negative effect reflects job displacement due to increased competition from Chinese imports. The magnitude suggests a 15-30% decline in manufacturing employment in high-exposure regions relative to low-exposure regions following WTO accession, which aligns with empirical literature on trade liberalization's employment effects in developed countries.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log manufacturing employment before and after 2001 between high and low trade exposure regions.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Regions with higher exposure to trade experienced a positive effect on manufacturing employment following China's WTO accession.
